subject.title: fix: forward response-frame meta to clients

question: After the branch is rebased, should Gateway protocol v4 accept optional top-level `res.meta`, or should response metadata be versioned or moved into a method-specific payload contract?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but the public response envelope currently rejects unknown top-level fields, so accepting this PR sets compatibility expectations for strict generated clients.

options.title: Accept additive `res.meta` after rebase
options.body: Port the patch to current main, keep `meta` optional and absent by default, and treat strict older-client rejection as an acceptable additive-v4 compatibility risk.

options.title: Require versioned envelope metadata
options.body: Pause the PR until a version-gated response-envelope contract is designed for strict clients.

options.title: Use method payload metadata instead
options.body: Reject top-level frame metadata and require handlers that need dedupe signals to expose them in method-specific payloads.

recommendation.title: Accept additive `res.meta` after rebase
recommendation.body: Port the patch to current main, keep `meta` optional and absent by default, and treat strict older-client rejection as an acceptable additive-v4 compatibility risk.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about Gateway protocol/release compatibility, and Vincent Koc has recent history on the shared handler type and release protocol surfaces.
